entry.title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
entry.summary: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.

entry.title: Mass Proxy Quality of Halo Properties in IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO Simulations: II. Galaxies, Stars, and Black Holes
entry.summary: We study the stellar, black hole, and satellite galaxy populations of group- and cluster-scale halos in the IllustrisTNG, TNG-Cluster, and FLAMINGO cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. We characterize the mass-conditioned scaling relations, covariance, conditional likelihoods, and mass proxy quality (MPQ) of integral properties within $R_{\rm 500c}$: total stellar mass ($M_{\star,\,\rm tot}$), brightest central galaxy stellar mass ($M_{\star,\,\rm BCG}$), intracluster light mass ($M_{\star,\,\rm ICL}$), total black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$), satellite occupation ($N_{\rm sat}$), and satellite velocity dispersion ($σ_{\rm sat,\,1D}$), at $z\in \{0,0.5,1,2\}$. While normalization differences of up to a factor of two emerge among simulations, many properties exhibit remarkably similar mass-localized slopes, intrinsic scatters, and MPQs across halo samples and redshifts. Correlations among stellar, satellite, and gas properties are generally consistent in sign and their dependence on halo mass and redshift, whereas those involving $M_{\rm BH}$ and $N_{\rm sat}$ show greater variation, particularly in TNG-Cluster. Conditional likelihoods are nearly lognormal for many properties, including $M_{\star,\,\rm tot}$, $N_{\rm sat}$, and $σ_{\rm sat,\,1D}$, while $M_{\star,\,\rm BCG}$ and $M_{\star,\,\rm ICL}$ are negatively skewed. Among the properties considered here, total stellar mass is the best mass proxy, with a halo mass scatter of $7$-$14\%$, followed by $N_{\rm sat}$ with a mass scatter of $9$-$18\%$. The consistent correlation behavior of $M_{\star,\,\rm ICL}$ highlights its potential for next-generation observational studies. Finally, $σ_{\rm sat,\,1D}$ exhibits highly consistent scaling, with mass-independent slope and scatter and a largely neutral correlation structure, suggesting that it is relatively insensitive to astrophysical complexity.

entry.title: Color-Kinematics Duality and the Double Copy in Curved Spacetimes
entry.summary: The double copy relates gravitational data to gauge-theory data, most sharply through color-kinematics duality for flat-space scattering amplitudes. This review surveys the extent to which this idea can be formulated beyond asymptotically flat backgrounds. After recalling the flat-space ingredients needed for comparison, we describe curved-space constructions for boundary correlators and scattering observables in AdS, dS, and other non-trivial backgrounds. We then review classical and field-level maps, including Kerr--Schild, Weyl, Cotton, twistor, and convolutional double copies. A separate part is devoted to self-dual sectors. Throughout, we emphasize both the common structures that survive from flat space and the obstructions introduced by curvature.

entry.title: A Star's Death by a Thousand Cuts: The Runaway Periodic Eruptions of AT2023uqm
entry.summary: Stars on bound orbits around a supermassive black hole may undergo repeated partial tidal disruption events (rpTDEs), producing periodic flares. While several candidates have been suggested, definitive confirmation of these events remains elusive. We report the discovery of AT2023uqm, a nuclear transient that has exhibited at least five periodic optical flares, making it only the second confirmed case of periodicity after ASASSN-14ko. Uniquely, the flares from AT2023uqm show a nearly exponential increase in energy--a "runaway" phenomenon signaling the star's progressive destruction. This behavior is consistent with rpTDEs of low-mass, main-sequence stars or evolved giant stars. Multiwavelength observations and spectroscopic analysis of the two most recent flares reinforce its interpretation as an rpTDE. Intriguingly, each flare displays a similar double-peaked structure, potentially originating from a double-peaked mass fallback rate or two discrete collisions per orbit. The extreme ratio of peak separation to orbital period draws attention to the possibility of a giant star being disrupted, which could be distinguished from a low-mass main-sequence star by its future mass-loss evolution. Our analysis demonstrates the power of rpTDEs to probe the properties of disrupted stars and the physical processes of tidal disruption, though it is currently limited by our knowledge of these events. AT2023uqm emerges as the most compelling rpTDE thus far, serving as a crucial framework for modeling and understanding these phenomena.

entry.title: Sharp null-energy lower bounds for Page-like entropy excursions in two-dimensional conformal field theory
entry.summary: We derive sharp lower bounds on the energy cost of Page-like entanglement entropy excursions in two-dimensional conformal field theory. For states satisfying the primary quantum null energy condition (QNEC), the positive null energy $E_+$ obeys a sharp lower bound with two branches separated by the threshold $ΔS=(c/6)\ln 2$. We also derive a sharp lower bound on the net energy $E_{\rm net}$, with a coefficient larger by a factor of two than the value quoted by Abdolrahimi and Page [Phys. Rev. D 92, 083005 (2015)] and, in the QNEC-saturating sector, we obtain a sharp lower bound on the negative energy $E_-$. The constants are sharp as infima over smooth conformal vacua. We determine the entropy profiles that minimize $E_+$ for general QNEC states and the one that minimizes $E_-$ in the saturating sector. Finally, for an excursion containing an infinite sequence of small sub-excursions within a finite duration, we derive a necessary condition for the total positive energy to remain finite, which is stronger than requiring the entropy to have finite total variation.

entry.title: The School on Gravity: from motion to commotion
entry.summary: Understanding the gravitational interaction is one of the great scientific endeavors of the 21st century. The Nobel Prize-winning discovery of gravitational waves in 2015, and subsequent detections by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration, have marked a revolutionary step forward in physics and astrophysics by opening an entirely new window for exploring the Universe. Future upgrades to these detectors, along with upcoming facilities such as LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and radio and optical instruments, promise other breakthrough discoveries that the next generation of scientists will need to interpret. The School on Gravity (22--26 June 2026, Copenhagen) aimed to introduce junior scientists--graduate students and advanced undergraduates with a background in general relativity--to a wide range of foundational topics in the exciting new field of gravitational-wave physics. Topics spanned from the theory of motion, to new challenges introduced by quantum physics, to the astrophysics of black holes and source modeling for gravitational-wave detectors. The School on Gravity took place at the legendary Auditorium A of the Niels Bohr Institute, inviting students and lecturers to challenge current paradigms in gravitational physics in the spirit of the quantum revolution that unfolded in this very room. These lecture notes aim at opening up those new ideas presented in Auditorium A to the rest of the scientific community.

entry.title: A Unified Scalar-Field Mechanism for the $H_0$, $S_8$ and Evolving Dark-Energy Tensions
entry.summary: We propose a unified scalar-field framework that addresses, within standard general relativity, three current cosmological anomalies: the $H_0$ tension, the mild preference for reduced late-time clustering ($S_8$), and recent indications of evolving dark energy. The model contains a single minimally coupled canonical scalar field evolving in a smooth potential composed of a localized bump superimposed on an exponential tail. The bump generates a transient pre-recombination energy injection that increases the expansion rate before last scattering, reduces the sound horizon, and shifts the CMB-inferred value of $H_0$ upward. After the field is released, its energy density rapidly redshifts through a kination-like phase, ensuring that the early modification does not persist as an unwanted late-time contribution. At low redshift, the exponential tail drives quintessence-like evolution, naturally yielding $w_0>-1$ and $w_a<0$ while suppressing linear structure growth and moving $S_8$ in the observationally preferred direction. The analysis shows explicitly how this smooth single-field potential can produce the required sequence of early enhancement, rapid dilution, and late-time thawing behavior.

entry.title: Compactly supported instability of Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metrics
entry.summary: On the Riemannian Schwarzschild--Tangherlini metric of dimension $n\geq 4$, we show that the destabilizing TT tensor of Ozuch lies in the image of the ``TT-tensor machine''. By continuity, it can then be approximated, in suitable weighted Sobolev spaces, by smooth compactly supported TT tensors, on which the stability quadratic form is still negative. This proves instability in the usual sense for noncompact manifolds. To our knowledge, no exact smooth compactly supported destabilizing TT tensor was known before, even in 4D.

entry.title: Integrable auxiliary field sigma model and the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations
entry.summary: We describe a family of two-dimensional metric deformations that preserve integrability. The seeds are (classically) conformal integrable field theories and the deformations are directly related to different classes of auxiliary field sigma models. We introduce a master action connecting deformations by Lie-algebra-valued auxiliary fields, the so-called $ν$-frame, to deformations by two Lorentz-charged scalars. These auxiliary scalar fields can be identified as Beltrami differentials of an auxiliary two-dimensional metric, providing a direct connection with the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations. For Weyl-invariant seed matter theories, the auxiliary metric sector is described by a reduced gravitational potential. We show that the resulting framework preserves classical Lax integrability whenever the seed matter theory admits a Lax representation of its equations of motion on a generic curved two-dimensional spacetime. Finally, within the Lorentz-invariant family and the zweibein deformations of conformal matter theories considered here, we identify $T\bar{T}$ as the only deformation that can be interpreted as a field-dependent coordinate transformation.

entry.title: Exploring non-Poisson satellite occupation in HOD models and its impact on 2- and 3-point galaxy clustering
entry.summary: Understanding the connection between galaxies and dark matter halos is a central challenge in modern cosmology. The Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) framework provides a widely used statistical description of how galaxies populate dark matter halos, enabling precise modelling of galaxy clustering. A common assumption in standard HOD models is that the number of satellite galaxies follows a Poisson distribution at fixed halo mass. In this work, we revisit this assumption and introduce the Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (CMP) distribution as a minimal extension of of the Poisson model, which add a single parameter, $ν$, to explore sub- and super-Poisson behaviour. We derive analytical approximations for the CMP expectation parameter $λ$ and develop a numerical scheme that smoothly connects small- and large-$λ$ regimes, achieving $\sim5\%$ accuracy for $0.5 < ν< 2$. Using the \texttt{HODDIES} package, we study the impact of non-Poisson satellite occupations on mock galaxy catalogues and clustering statistics. Variations in the variance of the satellite occupation significantly affect small-scale clustering, producing deviations of up to $10\%$ in projected clustering and $5\%$ in the monopole and quadrupole. We further investigate higher-order statistics using counts-in-cylinders (CiC) and the tree-level galaxy bispectrum. CiC statistics are highly sensitive to changes in the variance, with variations up to $\sim30\%$, while the tree-level galaxy bispectrum (in the Sugiyama basis) is only weakly affected ($<2\%$ up to $k_\mathrm{max} = 0.3$). These results suggest that non-Poisson satellite statistics are important for small-scale analyses, but should have a limited impact on cosmological constraints from power spectrum and bispectrum measurements using large scales $k_\mathrm{max} < 0.3$.

entry.title: Real versus Complex Fermion Bare Mass and Multi-Wall String Defect Annihilation
entry.summary: Particle physics models beyond the Standard Model often contain global symmetries to address various unanswered questions. However, a common criticism of theories based on global symmetries is that such symmetries are generally expected to be explicitly violated by gravitational effects at the Planck scale. In the case of a global $U(1)$ symmetry, this explicit breaking can reduce the symmetry to a discrete subgroup of $U(1)$, leading to the formation of cosmic strings attached to multiple domain walls (DWs). These DWs are usually cosmologically problematic, since their slow scaling behavior can eventually dominate the energy density of the Universe, giving rise to the well-known cosmological DW problem, which is strongly constrained by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis. In this work, we propose a mechanism for the annihilation of these DWs. If a fermion coupled to the symmetry-breaking scalar has a small bare mass, radiative corrections generate a temperature-dependent vacuum bias that drives DW collapse. As an example, we consider a majoron model with right-handed neutrinos, where gravity-induced operators produce a string-wall network. We show that a real bare Majorana mass is sufficient to induce complete DW annihilation for even-dimensional gravity-induced operators, whereas odd-dimensional operators require a complex bare Majorana mass whose phase lifts the residual vacuum degeneracy, enabling complete annihilation.

entry.title: Magnetic-field-induced detwinning of orientational domains in altermagnet $α$-MnTe: A single-crystal neutron diffraction study
entry.summary: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, which makes them promising for future spintronic and magnonic applications, but their macroscopic responses can be strongly reduced by domain averaging. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, three symmetry-related in-plane Néel-vector orientations and their time-reversal counterparts form six magnetic domain states, complicating both magnetic structure determination and measurements of the chiral magnon response. Using single-crystal neutron diffraction, we show that an in-plane field applied along the $[-1,1,0]$ direction produces a common magnetic domain orientation that saturates near $μ_0H=2$ T. A constrained refinement of 61 nuclear and magnetic reflections collected at 2 K and 2 T yields $\mathbf{M}\parallel[1,1,0]$, an ordered moment of $4.62(8)~μ_\mathrm{B}$ per Mn, and an orientational domain population at $r_A:r_B:r_C=0.97:0.03(5):0$ that is compatible with a nearly complete alignment of orientational domains. Furthermore, an abnormal behaviour in the temperature dependence of the selected reflections is observed in 60-88 K, its microscopic origin is discussed within the context of possible intrinsic piezomagnetic or magnetoelastic effects. Because unpolarized diffraction neither distinguishes domain repopulation from continuous Néel-vector rotation nor resolves time-reversal antiphase domains, the field-prepared state is a near-single-orientation state rather than a truly single-domain state. This non-contact domain control provides a practical complement to strain and field-cooling approaches for preparing well-defined magnetic states in bulk $α$-MnTe.

entry.title: Modelling Josephson Junctions with Boundary Conditions: Towards High-Fidelity Models for Superconducting Qubits
entry.summary: Josephson junctions are the central nonlinear element of superconducting qubits, yet their standard description is reached through a chain of approximations. We propose a purely quantum-mechanical model of the junction, formulated directly in Hilbert space: a charged particle moves on a one-dimensional loop, and the junction is a point at which the wave function obeys self-adjoint boundary conditions, labelled by a coupling strength $λ$, which controls the transparency of the junction, and a phase jump $δ$, which plays the role of the superconducting phase difference. For a loop with a single junction we solve the spectral problem and show that the ground-state momentum expectation, identified with the supercurrent, factorises exactly as $\langle\hat{p}_0\rangle = I_c(δ,λ)\sinδ$. For opaque junctions $I_c$ becomes independent of $δ$ and the first Josephson relation $I=I_c\sinδ$ is recovered; for strongly attractive coupling, where the ground state is bound to the junction, the $\sinδ$ law is also recovered, but with an exponentially suppressed amplitude. For more transparent junctions, however, the model \emph{predicts} deviations from the pure $\sinδ$ law: $I_c$ acquires a dependence on $δ$ already at order $λ^{-2}$, compatible with the higher Josephson harmonics recently found necessary to describe superconducting qubit spectra, and a fully transparent contact yields a current linear in $δ$. When the phase varies in time, a gauge transformation shows that the voltage drop across the junction is proportional to $\dotδ$, so that the second Josephson relation emerges without being imposed. The boundary-condition approach thus reproduces both Josephson relations from first principles and predicts corrections to them, offering a route towards higher-fidelity models of superconducting qubits.

entry.title: Probing black holes with equivariant localization
entry.summary: We introduce equivariant localization as a method for computing the action of probe branes in supergravity backgrounds. We apply it to supersymmetric probe D3-branes in type IIB supersymmetric spacetimes obtained by uplifting the Kerr-Newman-AdS$_5$ black hole on a toric Sasaki-Einstein space. Depending on the cycles they wrap, such branes represent non-perturbative corrections to or defect operator insertions in the superconformal index of a large family of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ quiver superconformal field theories. The resulting action reduces to equivariant integrals and can be evaluated entirely from toric data.

entry.title: Temperature evolution of spin dynamics in extended Kitaev models within an Abrikosov fermion theory beyond mean field
entry.summary: The $S=1/2$ Kitaev model provides an exactly solvable setting in which spin fractionalization produces itinerant Majorana fermions coupled to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge field. In realistic Kitaev magnets, however, non-Kitaev interactions break integrability and make their finite-temperature dynamics difficult to calculate. We develop a finite-temperature parton mean-field theory based on the Abrikosov-fermion representation and incorporate the effects of exchange interactions through the random phase approximation to calculate the dynamical spin structure factor. For the pure Kitaev model, the method reproduces a strong, nearly dispersionless peak at a finite low energy together with a broad continuum at higher energies. It also reproduces the momentum dependence of the dynamical spin structure factor and its temperature evolution, including the downward shift of the low-energy spectral weight, in qualitative agreement with continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo calculations. Within the present theory, the contraction of the continuum is traced to the temperature-induced reduction of the bond amplitudes, which narrows the parton bands and compresses the two-parton phase space. For ferromagnetic Kitaev coupling, the energy of the low-energy peak is minimized at the $Γ$ point for a ferromagnetic Heisenberg interaction and maximized there for an antiferromagnetic interaction. In the ferromagnetic Kitaev-$Γ$ model, the static response develops a finite-momentum softening, indicating an instability toward the period-three magnetic order reported in numerical studies. For uniform-ferromagnetic states selected by a $[111]$ magnetic field, we find that a broad parton continuum coexists with magnonlike dispersive structures, producing spectral features consistent with a spinon-to-magnon crossover.

entry.title: Detecting redshift space distortions with forthcoming 21cm intensity maps from MeerKLASS
entry.summary: Redshift space distortions (RSD) provide a powerful measurement of structure formation in modern cosmology. In this work, we explore the potential of 21cm intensity mapping with the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) to detect RSD and probe gravity within the redshift range of MeerKAT's UHF band ($0.4<z<1.45$). Using simulated sky observations, we examine the impact from observational effects caused by blind foreground removal and MeerKAT's primary beam, plus $k$-cuts to the measurements. With a multipole expansion formalism, we demonstrate how the quadrupole of the HI power spectrum can be modelled and also show how a foreground transfer function can reconstruct the distorted signal. With 1,115 deg$^2$ of simulated MeerKLASS observations at $0.4<z<1.0$, our proposed analysis pipeline reveals a $6.7σ$ detection of an RSD-induced quadrupole relative to one caused by anisotropic observational effects alone. We also explore parameter inference with the full MeerKLASS 10,000 deg$^2$ survey. Within forecasts, we demonstrate how a tomographic analysis across the full UHF redshift range can be leveraged to address certain parameter degeneracies with e.g. the HI bias ($b_{\rm HI}$) and cosmic density of HI ($Ω_{\rm HI}$). By adopting a redshift-dependent model for the bias and HI density combined with simulation-informed priors, we demonstrate how degeneracies can be alleviated, and indicate the potential for MeerKLASS to reach competitive precision on simple probes of modified gravity.

entry.title: Dualities, symmetries and the elliptic genus of 2d (0,2) SCFTs
entry.summary: While naively simpler than its higher dimensional cousins, 2d physics still has its own share of puzzles. An example of this is instances of dualities of $(0,2)$ theories, passing all consistency checks save for a mismatch in global symmetry. This is common when said duality can be motivated by dimensional reduction of a duality of 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories where said symmetry emerges in 2d, often from an anomalous 4d symmetry. It is commonly believed that these symmetries are broken in the 2d theory, though often the mechanism for such breaking is not understood. We examine various appearances of this phenomenon and show that in these cases the elliptic genus shows signs of the presence of marginal operators that can break these symmetries. Interestingly, these operators do not appear perturbatively but emerge from the calculation, raising the question of what operators the $(0,2)$ elliptic genus actually counts. This provides a potential mechanism to overcome the discrepancy in symmetry, though we point out some potential subtleties.

entry.title: Flip-Flop Shocks and Tori in Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton Accretion onto Rotating Kerr-Weyl Black Holes and Their Quasi-Periodic Variability
entry.summary: We present GRHD simulations of Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion onto a rotating black hole in Weyl conformal gravity, described by the Kerr-Weyl metric. The equatorial flow is evolved for spins a=0.9M and a=0.5M and several Weyl coefficients, which enter through an effective curvature parameter k, and is compared with Kerr runs sharing the same setup. For the k considered, the horizon, ISCO and test-particle frequencies differ from Kerr by at most ~2%. However, the curvature term grows as kr^2 and acts at the accretion radius R_acc. The flow is controlled by one quantity, eta=|k|R_acc^3/M, the ratio of curvature-induced to Newtonian acceleration at R_acc. For eta<~0.03 a stable shock cone forms, indistinguishable from Kerr. For eta~0.2-0.3 the anti-de Sitter-like term traps shocked gas behind the black hole and drives persistent flip-flop oscillations. For eta>~1.6 the cone is destroyed and an oscillating torus forms. Spin modifies only the inner few gravitational radii and does not change the regime. In strongly deviating models the mean accretion rate is 1.7-3 times the Kerr value and varies by 20-60% rms, versus 0.1-1% in Kerr-like flows. The power spectra show global QPOs with fundamentals at 2.9-4.8 Hz for a 10 Msun black hole, with harmonic ladders whose 3:2 and 2:1 ratios come from one non-sinusoidal oscillation, not resonances. These lie in the low-frequency QPO band and are unrelated to test-particle frequencies (~70-200 Hz). They scale as f_0=xi f_K(R_acc), with xi~0.7-1.1 for stable cones and xi~0.23-0.38 for flip-flop and torus regimes. Strong oscillations would be detectable within seconds for a bright Galactic source. The required |k| exceeds galactic-rotation-curve values by 18-36 orders of magnitude, so a detected shock-driven QPO would measure a local deviation from Kerr, and its absence would constrain |k|.

entry.title: Uniform-Charge-Density $d$-Wave Superconductivity in the Pure $t$-$J$ Model at $1/8$ Doping on an Infinite Cylinder
entry.summary: The ground state of the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at $1/8$ hole doping has been the subject of a long-standing controversy, with conflicting numerical reports of stripe order versus superconductivity. Here, we address this debate using the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) method, which optimizes the wave function directly in the thermodynamic limit along the cylinder axis and eliminates the boundary pinning effects that can arise in finite-cylinder calculations. On an infinite cylinder of circumference $L_y = 8$, we find a uniform-charge-density $d$-wave superconducting ground state with quasi-long-range pairing correlations. The dominant pairing occurs at zero center-of-mass momentum, while no sizable finite-momentum pairing component is detected. Twisted-boundary-condition calculations reveal a finite superconducting phase stiffness, with the order-parameter phase winding smoothly to follow the applied flux, providing an independent probe of the robustness of the superconductivity. Moreover, both charge and spin correlations decay rapidly, with no signatures of long-range stripe or magnetic order, in contrast to an $L_y=6$ cylinder at $1/6$ doping where the same method readily identifies stripe order. Our results provide methodologically distinct evidence in the long-standing stripe--superconductivity debate in the pure $t$-$J$ model and reveal uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in a minimal model of doped Mott insulators.

entry.title: On the quantum statistical relation and the covariant phase space Hamiltonian
entry.summary: We show how the covariant phase space Hamiltonian can be constructed in theories in which some of the fields have gauge freedoms. The addition to the action of boundary terms that guarantee the well-posedness of a variational principle and its exact gauge invariance for the prescribed boundary conditions turn out to be essential in this construction. The same ingredients are essential in the use of the action in the framework of Gibbons and Hawking's Euclidean approach to Quantum Gravity and we show how the on-shell action constructed with a Lagrangian with those properties can be expressed in terms of the covariant phase space Hamiltonian. We compute the Hamiltonian of several theories, one of which has Chern--Simons terms, using our prescription and show that, in black-hole backgrounds, the Hamiltonian gives directly the quantum statistical relation including terms related to non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.

entry.title: Absence of Continuous Spin Particles in Superstring Theory
entry.summary: The study of continuous spin particles, as general low-energy implications of relativity and quantum mechanics, has intensified in recent years with potential experimental signatures. In this note we show that these particles are absent in perturbative super-string theories, generalising a result in arXiv:1302.4771 to the supersymmetric case. This stands out as a general low-energy prediction of all perturbative superstring constructions.

entry.title: Novel $\mathcal{N}=2$ higher-spin supercurrents
entry.summary: We study cubic interactions of $\mathcal N=2$ massless integer-spin gauge supermultiplets in harmonic superspace. We construct the complete class of abelian $(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{s_1},\mathbf{s_2})$ cubic vertices with the minimal number of space-time derivatives. Such vertices exist only for $\mathbf{s}\geq \mathbf{s_1}+\mathbf{s_2}$ and universally take the form of the gauge prepotential coupled to the conserved higher-spin supercurrent. For~$\mathbf{s_1}\neq\mathbf{s_2}$, we find the novel complex principal supercurrent, whose real and imaginary parts generate the parity-invariant and the parity-breaking interactions, respectively. The supercurrents are constructed from gauge-invariant $\mathcal N=2$ higher-spin Weyl supertensors associated with the spin-$\mathbf{s_1}$ and spin-$\mathbf{s_2}$ gauge multiplets. These supertensors are defined in terms of unconstrained higher-spin analytic prepotentials. We also derive the complete set of conserved component higher-spin currents associated with the $(s,s_1,s_2)$ vertices, including both traceless currents and currents with the non-vanishing trace.

entry.title: Linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ conformal supergravity in the harmonic approach
entry.summary: Using the harmonic superspace approach, we construct the superconformal harmonic action for $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl supermultiplet. The fundamental objects of the theory are unconstrained analytic potentials $h^{++α\dotα}, h^{++α+}, h^{++\dotα+}, h^{(+4)}$, which distinguishes our construction among the previously known ones. An important role is played by the ``half-analyticity'' conditions introduced in arXiv:2407.08524 [hep-th]. The structure of the harmonic linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl action to large extent repeats the structure of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Maxwell action, which suggests a conjecture on the possible structure of the complete nonlinear $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl theory action in the harmonic superspace. We provide a detailed study of the rigid superconformal properties of the proposed action and prove its invariance in both harmonic and chiral superspaces. First steps are also undertaken towards constructing the nonlinear $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl action, based on an analogy with $\mathcal{N}=2$ Maxwell action just mentioned and a generalization of the concept of half-analyticity to curved harmonic superspace.

entry.title: Interplay of disorder and spin liquid physics in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet YbZn2GaO5
entry.summary: YbZn2GaO5 has recently emerged as a structurally ideal triangular-lattice antiferromagnet and a promising candidate for hosting a U(1) Dirac quantum spin-liquid (QSL) ground state. However, signatures of broadened crystal electric field (CEF) excitations have raised questions about potential site disorder and its impact on the intrinsic spin dynamics. In this study, we employ 71Ga nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and muon spin relaxation (muSR) to microscopically probe both the structural and magnetic properties of YbZn2GaO5. NMR spectra reveal two inequivalent 71Ga sites and a broad distribution of quadrupolar frequencies, providing clear evidence of Ga$^{3+}$/Zn$^{2+}$ site mixing and local CEF randomness. The NMR spin-lattice relaxation rate exhibits, down to 1.3~K, a power-law temperature dependence, consistent with persisting spin dynamics below the exchange energy scale in a frustrated magnet. Complementary muSR measurements further show that the spin dynamics persist down to 30mK, with no signs of spin freezing. Together, these results establish that YbZn2GaO5 presents substantial structural disorder, while the persistence of dynamic spin fluctuations down to the lowest temperatures may indicate the survival of QSL-like excitations despite such disorder.

entry.title: On the magnetic counterpart of the Uehling correction
entry.summary: In this work, we investigate the magnetic properties of the quantum vacuum in the context of QED. We calculate the quantum relativistic correction of virtual particle-anti-particle pair creation to the field of a classical point-like idealized magnet. Using such correction, we find the induced currents stemming from the effect of the polarization of the vacuum, which behaves like a paramagnetic medium. We also calculate the correction to the electric dipole potential and show that the well-known symmetry between the classical fields of point electric and magnetic dipoles is broken at the quantum level. Lastly, to illustrate possible applications of our findings, we briefly discuss the effect of the corrections obtained here in the context of neutron-neutron scattering and the hyperfine splitting for hydrogen-like atoms.

entry.title: Chiral Symmetries in the Standard Model of Particle Physics and its Extensions
entry.summary: Chiral gauge theories are a central focus of research in theoretical particle physics due to the parity symmetry breaking observed in the Standard Model. Left-Right Symmetric Models (LRM) explain the breaking of parity through a Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism, predicting new $W_R$ and $Z_R$ gauge bosons. The absence of direct BSM physics detection at the LHC has driven research towards precision observables and Effective Field Theories (EFTs), particularly the SMEFT framework. Precision radiative calculations in chiral theories using dimensional regularization require a $D$-dimensional $γ_5$ prescription, such as the mathematically consistent Breitenlohner-Maison-'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme. However, this scheme introduces gauge symmetry-breaking terms that obstruct Slavnov-Taylor identities. A primary objective of this thesis is to provide a pedagogical introduction to cancelling these spurious anomalies via algebraic renormalization, and to derive the one-loop symmetry-restoring finite counterterms required to renormalize the four-fermion operators of the $ν$SMEFT. Furthermore, the thesis explores UV completions like LRMs embedded in other BSM theories like the Grand Unified Theories. This embedding implies that no discrete symmetries remain at the TeV scale and allows LRMs to be treated as EFTs with the minimal scalar content needed to perform the Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism. The second main objective is to derive robust lower bounds on the masses of the new gauge bosons and the LR scale using collider observables. This analysis is performed for both the effective and traditional LRMs, ensuring that the results are independent of other parameters of the theory.

entry.title: General relativity and its modifications as effective field theories of $GL(4)$ breaking
entry.summary: We discuss General Relativity and some of its modifications as effective field theories of the breaking of the affine general linear group using the coset approach and the Maurer-Cartan form. While the ultimate goal is to break the symmetry down to the Lorentz subgroup, we argue that there are three interesting breaking cascades in which the affine general linear group is first broken to a larger subgroup that contains the Lorentz group. In all cases, the breaking of translations always generates Goldstone modes that can be interpreted as metric degrees of freedom. We argue that the effective field theories that emerge as a result of the different breaking patterns are all dynamically equivalent at the lowest order of the derivative expansion, e.g., using Einstein-Hilbert-like actions, but can differ beyond the leading order.

entry.title: Gravitational wave echoes as probes of the maximum mass of strange stars in quadratic curvature-matter coupled gravity
entry.summary: Gravitational wave astronomy provides a powerful avenue for probing exotic compact stars. Recent analyses of GW170817 have reported possible post-merger gravitational wave echoes with a significance of $4.2σ$ and a dominant frequency near $72,\text{Hz}$. Such echoes may arise from ultracompact remnants possessing photon spheres that partially trap gravitational perturbations. In general relativity, photon-sphere formation requires the stellar compactness to lie between one-third and four-ninths, a condition difficult to achieve with realistic equations of state. Here, we investigate this possibility in quadratic curvature gravity with non-minimal matter coupling, considering strange stars described by the MIT bag model equation of state. By solving the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we obtain mass-radius relations and identify configurations capable of supporting photon spheres and gravitational wave echoes. The modified Buchdahl limit permits more compact stellar solutions, while photon-sphere constraints restrict the viable parameter space. We find that increasing the bag constant reduces the maximum mass and echo time, shifting the echo frequency toward the kHz regime. The echo constraints impose more stringent maximum mass-radius limits than hydrostatic equilibrium, suggesting revised maximum mass bounds for strange stars. We further compute the critical impact parameter and eikonal quasi-normal modes, demonstrating how modified gravity parameters systematically alter the photon-sphere radius and associated observational signatures. These results establish post-merger strange stars as potential GW echo sources and highlight echoes, optical shadows, and QNMs as complementary probes of modified gravity for next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.

entry.title: Lee--Yang Zeros and Pseudocritical Drift in J-Q Néel Antiferromagnet--Valence-Bond Solid Transitions
entry.summary: Square-lattice J-Q models provide a sign-problem-free setting for probing the quantum phase transition between Néel antiferromagnet and columnar valence-bond solid. We analyze this transition through the scaling of Lee--Yang zeros, computed within stochastic series expansion quantum Monte Carlo by reweighting configurations sampled near criticality in the presence of complex source fields. Benchmark studies of the dimerized Heisenberg model and the checkerboard J-Q model validate the method, yielding stable \(\mathrm{O}(3)\) critical scaling in the former and clear spacetime-volume scaling in the latter, as expected for a first-order transition. Applying the same analysis to the J-Q models, we find a pronounced and systematic drift of the leading-zero scaling with increasing system size, consistent with an extended pseudocritical regime. The Lee--Yang scaling implies an effective scaling dimension \(Δ_φ\) of the \(\mathrm{SO}(5)\) order-parameter field that decreases with size and is consistent with vanishing in the thermodynamic limit. Such behavior lies below the scalar unitarity bound of any unitary relativistic conformal field theory in \(2{+}1\) dimensions and enforces inverse spacetime-volume scaling of the zeros, the hallmark of a first-order transition. These results support a weakly first-order interpretation of the Néel--VBS transition and establish the finite-size Lee--Yang zeros as a sensitive, symmetry-resolved diagnostic of pseudocriticality and transition order in the J-Q family.

entry.title: Quantum Fisher Information of Driven-Dissipative Systems from Keldysh Path Integrals
entry.summary: Driven-dissipative many-body quantum systems can be exploited in quantum enhanced sensing protocols. Here, non-classical correlations may allow one to reach a measurement precision that surpasses the standard quantum limit. The relevant figure of merit for assessing such quantum advantage is the quantum Fisher information (QFI). In a many-body setting its computation is challenging as it requires knowledge of the full system-environment state. Here we make use of a field-theoretical approach, which is particularly well suited for systems with many degrees of freedom. In particular, we exploit that the QFI can be linked to a Keldysh path-integral. This route leads to a semiclassical expression of the QFI, which is obtained through a controlled expansion in the so-called quantum fields. We benchmark the framework on three systems of increasing complexity: the driven-dissipative harmonic oscillator, the boundary time crystal - which becomes semiclassical at large system sizes - and a two-dimensional array of collectively emitting atoms. We assess in which parameter regimes the semiclassical description holds and gives access to system sizes beyond the reach of exact methods.

entry.title: HAMCOR: A physics-driven Hamiltonian framework for inferring AGN coronal geometry from X-ray reverberation lags
entry.summary: We present HAMCOR (Hamiltonian-based AGN Multi-constraint CORonal inference framework), a geometry-agnostic method for inferring the X-ray coronal structure of accreting black holes using reverberation-lag measurements. Unlike conventional template-fitting approaches, HAMCOR reframes coronal geometry inference as the ground-state selection of a physical Hamiltonian. The corona is represented as a discrete emissivity distribution over a cylindrical grid, and its geometry emerges from five competing physical constraints: magnetic coherence, lag consistency, illumination consistency, pair-production stability, and energy budget feasibility. Minimisation is performed via projected gradient descent with Armijo backtracking line search on the probability simplex. We validate HAMCOR on three synthetic geometries (lamppost, column, ring) using the same grid as the real-data fits, recovering spatial correlations rho = 0.24, 0.50, 0.12 and fractional lag errors below 24 per cent. A hyperparameter sensitivity analysis confirms robustness over more than one order of magnitude in the coupling constants. We apply HAMCOR to five sources spanning seven orders of magnitude in black hole mass: four AGN observed with XMM-Newton (Mrk 335, 1H 0707-495, IRAS 13224-3809, MCG-6-30-15) and the stellar-mass black hole binary Cyg X-1 (M_bh = 14.8 M_sun), recovering consistent extended disc-corona geometries across the full mass range. We further present a multi-epoch analysis of Mrk 335 across five XMM-Newton observations (2006-2019), revealing that the coronal centroid remains stable at (R_c, z_c) ~ (6.3, 0.5) r_g across flux states spanning a factor of ~15 in reverberation lag amplitude, arguing against a collapsing or expanding lamppost. Schwarzschild-Shapiro delay corrections amount to ~79 per cent of the flat-spacetime lag on average; the recovered spatial morphology is robust to this correction.

entry.title: Finite-momentum superconductivity with singlet-triplet mixing in an altermagnetic metal: A pairing instability analysis
entry.summary: We analyze the pairing instability of an altermagnetic metal on a square lattice driven by an attractive nearest-neighbor interaction. This interaction enables multiple pairing channels, including even-parity extended $s$-wave and $d$-wave states, as well as two odd-parity $p$-wave channels. We verify that altermagnetic spin-splitting in the single-particle dispersion gives rise to finite-momentum pairing between electrons with unlike spins, in agreement with earlier predictions. Quite unexpectedly, this pairing typically emerges across multiple channels with mixed parity. Consequently, the resulting finite-momentum Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconducting phase is expected to exhibit a multi-component order parameter featuring singlet-triplet mixing. We examine several forms of altermagnetism, specifically $d_{xy}$-wave and $d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$-wave altermagnetic couplings, and present the corresponding phase diagrams. Additionally, we study triplet pairing between electrons with identical spins and find that it always occurs at zero center-of-mass momentum. Although it is unfavorable in the regime of weak altermagnetic coupling and low electron filling, it can dominate the phase diagram when the altermagnetic coupling is sufficiently strong. The influence of on-site attractive interactions on mixed-parity pairing is also explored.

entry.title: Particle production from bubble collisions
entry.summary: Collisions of ultra-relativistic bubbles during cosmological phase transitions can produce particles much heavier than the transition scale. Previous analyses modelled this process as the off-shell decay of the scalar background. We show that its results parametrically overestimate hard particle production and depend on the gauge choice and the coordinate choice in field space. We propose an alternative formalism, analogous to the partonic description of high-energy collisions. In the ultra-relativistic limit, the colliding bubbles undergo nearly free passage and hard production arises from on-shell scatterings among the quanta constituting the Lorentz-contracted walls. We apply this approach to heavy scalar, fermion, and vector particle production, and study the implications for dark matter, leptogenesis, graviton production and primordial gravitational waves.

entry.title: Extreme mass ratio inspirals from the Hills mechanism, The eccentricity distribution of Hills EMRIs in LISA
entry.summary: Extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are promising sources for future space-based gravitational-wave detectors. We investigate EMRIs produced through the Hills mechanism, in which a stellar-mass black-hole binary (BBH) is tidally separated by a massive black hole (MBH), leaving one component bound to it. We present the first self-consistent modelling of this channel, combining an orbit-averaged Fokker-Planck treatment of the nuclear star cluster (NSC), three-body modelling of the binary-MBH encounter, Monte Carlo evolution of captured black holes (BHs), and fully relativistic EMRI trajectories to follow the evolution from binary supply down to final plunge. We find that Hills EMRIs are substantially more circular than classical EMRIs formed through two-body relaxation. For an MBH of $4 \times 10^6 M_\odot$ and circular, equal-mass BBHs of $20 M_\odot$ with initial separation of $0.1$ AU, EMRI mean eccentricities are approximately $0.097$ at our adopted LISA-band entry threshold and $0.034$ at plunge, compared with $0.478$ and $0.228$, respectively, for classical EMRIs. Of the initial BBHs, approximately $0.4$ per cent become EMRIs, whereas approximately $60$ per cent of captured BHs do. For comparable NSC initial compact-object mass, we find approximately $1.6 \times 10^{-8}$ Hills EMRIs per year per galaxy, approximately $12$ per cent of the classical EMRI yield. The Hills channel contribution to the overall eccentricity distribution depends strongly on the binary mass fraction in NSCs. We discuss implications for identifying EMRI formation channels with LISA and for quasi-periodic eruptions.

entry.title: Observing the Peculiar Acceleration of our Solar System with Quasar Proper Motions
entry.summary: We measured the proper motion dipole of quasars observed by \textit{Gaia} to determine the acceleration of the Solar System with respect to the quasar rest frame. We characterised the full angular power spectrum of the proper motion field using the pseudo-$C_\ell$ formalism and employed simulation-based inference to jointly constrain the dipole and higher multipole power. Cross-correlation with the \textit{Gaia} scanning strategy, stellar density and stellar proper motion maps was used to diagnose the origin of systematic power beyond the dipole. We applied this framework to both the \textit{Gaia} EDR3 quasar catalogue and the Quaia catalogue. The inferred acceleration is consistent with the previous determination, but the credible intervals widen by factors of 1.5 to 5 when higher-multipole degeneracies are properly marginalised, indicating that previous uncertainty estimates were optimistic. Our best estimate, based on the Quaia catalogue, is ($g_x,\,g_y,\,g_z$) = $\left(1.01^{+0.72}_{-0.72}, \,-4.94^{+0.54}_{-0.55},\,-2.13^{+0.58}_{-0.58}\right) \;\rm μas \,yr^{-1}$. This corresponds to an amplitude of $5.55_{-0.53}^{+0.54}\,\rm \;μas\,yr^{-1}$, where $\mathbf{g} = \mathbf{a}/c$ is the Solar System acceleration expressed as a proper motion drift in equatorial coordinates. The inferred acceleration is directed towards $(l,\, b) = \left(11.71^{+7.0}_{-6.8},\, -9.01^{+7.0}_{-6.9}\right)^\circ$, equivalently $(α,\, δ) = \left(281.39^{+7.8}_{-8.0},\, -22.93^{+6.5}_{-6.2}\right)^\circ$. This is in good agreement with a Galactic centre--dominated acceleration. The acceleration components show no significant dependence on source redshift, providing further evidence of the acceleration's kinematic origin.

entry.title: Codimension-Zero Holographic Complexity and Spectral Three-Point Correlators
entry.summary: Holographic complexity is expected to capture the linear growth of black hole interiors, with quantum corrections ultimately leading to a late-time saturation. We develop a spectral formulation of holographic complexity measures associated with codimension-zero bulk regions in the framework of the complexity=anything proposal. The corresponding generating function of complexity is governed by three-point correlation functions of the density of states, establishing a direct connection between bulk geometric observables and nonperturbative Euclidean spacetime wormholes. We find that the codimension-zero holographic complexity reduces to the sum of two codimension-one contributions and exhibits a universal time evolution, characterized by an exponentially long regime of linear growth followed by saturation at the Heisenberg time. The late-time plateau is a direct result of the spectral level repulsion, a generic feature of quantum chaotic systems, thereby providing a universal mechanism for the saturation of holographic complexity. We also develop a complementary operator interpretation, in which Euclidean wormhole corrections render the semiclassical basis of fixed-complexity states overcomplete. Constructing a complete orthonormal basis then yields well-defined holographic complexity operators that reproduce the same universal time evolution. Our results establish a unified connection among black hole interiors, chaotic spectral statistics, and Euclidean wormholes in quantum gravity.

entry.title: Resistive alignment of a black-hole magnetosphere
entry.summary: Recent numerical simulations have shown that black-hole magnetospheres evolve rapidly toward alignment between the magnetic axis and spin axis but the physical origin of this process has remained unclear. We develop an analytic theory of this alignment within resistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics. Taking the slow-spin Blandford-Znajek monopole solution as the exterior magnetic field, we reduce the induction equation to a relaxation equation for the current-sheet inclination angle. Our analysis shows that alignment results from second-order spin effects in the Blandford-Znajek solution combined with explicit resistive dissipation. We test this prediction using resistive-GRMHD simulations at several spins and resistivities and find a regime in which the measured late-time secular decay agrees quantitatively with the analytic prediction.

entry.title: Confining Random Potential Quantum Mechanics for Jackiw-Teitelboim Gravity
entry.summary: We formulate perturbative Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity as an ensemble of ordinary one-dimensional Hamiltonians with a confining random potential. The leading profile reproduces the disk density of states, while connected cumulants of a single master field encode the topological expansion. After formulating the cumulant power counting required by the topological expansion, we show that the cumulants reproduce all genus-zero multi-boundary amplitudes $\mathcal Z_{0,n}$. At higher genus, we show that a renormalization scheme can be chosen consistently order by order so that imposing one-boundary polynomiality recursively reproduces the perturbative JT string equation and yields the standard JT one-boundary amplitudes $\mathcal Z_{g,1}$. The framework provides a self-contained finite-$S_0$ quantum dynamics with a discrete spectrum and unitary real time evolution, beyond a mere rewriting of the matrix integral. The same confining dynamics also underlies late-time saturation and the dynamical avoidance of the would-be black hole singularity, as shown in our earlier work.

entry.title: The Casimir energy in Maxwell-Chern-Simons electrodynamics with various perfect electric or magnetic boundary condition combinations
entry.summary: We investigate the Casimir effect between two parallel wires in $(2+1)D$ Maxwell-Chern-Simons (MCS) electrodynamics under different boundary conditions and separated by a distance $L$. Using a functional approach in which the boundary constraints are implemented by auxiliary fields localized on the wires, we integrate out the gauge field and derive an effective boundary theory whose functional determinant allows us to compute the Casimir energy. We consider perfect electric conductor (PEC), perfect magnetic conductor (PMC), and infinitely permeable (PMC2) boundary conditions. For two PEC wires, we recover the known MCS result and show that it coincides with the result obtained in the Abelian limit of the Curci-Ferrari (CF) model, implying that the Casimir effect in this case probes the photon mass $μ$ but not its origin. The same energy is obtained for two PMC2 wires. In sharp contrast, the Casimir energy vanishes identically for the covariant PMC condition in MCS theory, both for PMC-PMC and PEC-PMC. Since this cancellation does not occur in the CF model, it could provide a signature of the topological origin of the photon mass in $(2+1)D$. Finally, the PEC-PMC2 case yields a non-vanishing Casimir force and reproduces the known result for a perfectly conducting wire facing an infinitely permeable one. Interestingly enough, we show that for PEC-PMC2, the Casimir force in the MCS theory is smaller than the one of the CF model for any $L,μ>0$. Our results thus show that, depending on the boundary conditions, the Casimir effect could probe not only the photon mass but also reveal signatures of its origin.

entry.title: The point-particle-limit effective-source approach for computing gravitational self-force in the Lorenz gauge
entry.summary: The traditional effective-source method is hampered by complex analytical expressions and the inherent smoothness limit, which incur high computational costs and complicate implementation. To overcome these limitations, we introduce the point-particle-limit effective source method, which analytically takes the size of the effective source to zero, thereby transforming the problem into a well-defined jump condition of retarded metric field at the particle position governed by the local singular field. This formulation naturally pairs with a discontinuous Galerkin scheme, whose inherent capacity for accommodating solution discontinuities enables highly accurate enforcement of the jump conditions. We apply both the traditional and point-particle-limit effective source method to calculate the time-domain gravitational metric perturbation and gravitational self-force in the Lorenz gauge on a point particle in a circular orbit around a Schwarzschild black hole. The comparison of numerical results shows the excellent advantage of the point-particle-limit effective source method, which validates the correctness and efficiency of the point-particle-limit effective source method and thereby establishes a numerical foundation for computing generic geodesic orbits or long-time self-consistent orbital evolution.

entry.title: Boundary Energy Density and Null Propagation in Global AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$
entry.summary: We study how bulk propagation in global AdS$_3$ is reflected in boundary energy densities of the dual CFT$_2$ on the cylinder. A key feature of the global geometry, which is absent in the Poincaré-patch description, is that a null excitation emitted from the boundary reaches the antipodal boundary point after $Δτ=π$ and returns to the original boundary point after $Δτ=2π$. We show that the CFT energy density reproduces this sequence through two chiral peaks that move along the boundary light-cone directions, meet at the antipodal point, and return to the original point after one global period. For a wave-packet state, the leading energy density consists of two chiral peaks moving along the boundary light-cone directions; their relative weights encode the impact parameter of the corresponding bulk null ray. For a state constructed from an operator of large conformal dimension with a Euclidean time regulator (LCD state), the exact cylinder stress tensor gives two periodic chiral pulses moving along the boundary light-cone directions. These pulses reach the antipodal point and return to the original point at the same global times as the radial null geodesic in the bulk. Thus the boundary energy density provides a time-dependent boundary profile that reflects characteristic global features of null propagation in AdS$_3$.

entry.title: Pressure and Size Dependence of Roton Emission and Vortex Creation by Moving Objects in He~II in $T \to 0$ Limit: Generalized Nonlocal Gross-Pitaevskii Model
entry.summary: In the framework of generalized, nonlocal Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) model, we study numerically the pressure- and size-dependent mechanisms of roton emission and vortex nucleation by objects moving in superfluid $^4$He. As far as the authors are aware, this is the first attempt to analyze the pressure dependence of these mechanisms and the associated critical velocities within a single theoretical framework. For each of several pressures in the range from 0 to the solidification pressure of $\approx25$~bar, we chose the parameters of the interatomic interaction potential such that the resulting excitation spectrum for the generalized, nonlocal GP equation approximates fairly accurately the pressure-dependent dispersion curve determined experimentally by Godfrin \textit{et al.}, Phys. Rev. B \textbf{103}, 104516 (2021). In the two-dimensional approximation, for circular obstacles (disks) moving in quiescent $^4$He, we calculated two critical velocities -- one corresponding to the roton emission and the other to the nucleation of quantized vortices -- as functions of pressure and the obstacle's size. We also comment briefly on three-dimensional simulations of the roton emission and vortex nucleation by moving spherical obstacles.

entry.title: Ultrafast laser-stimulated field emission from a metal: a non-equilibrium Green's functions approach
entry.summary: Ultrafast laser-assisted field emission from metallic nanotips is a promising route for generating coherent electron pulses. However, existing theoretical models often neglect many-body strong correlation effects in the emitter's electronic structure and its response to the optical field. In this work, we propose a theoretical framework based on the non-equilibrium Green's function formalism to simulate the out-of-equilibrium electron dynamics across a strongly driven matter-vacuum interface, in a one-dimensional model. Treating the tip-vacuum coupling perturbatively, we find that the interplay between strong-field emission and multi-photon emission regimes can be described in terms of a filtering of the emitter's local density of occupied states through field-dressed vacuum propagators. By including electron-electron interactions via the second-Born approximation, we show that correlation-induced modifications in the electronic structure are directly transferred to the far-field spectrum. Finally, by self-consistently solving the Dyson equation at the interface, we uncover a dynamic back-action regime driven by the optical field, characterized by a periodic polarization of the emitter, which reshapes the far-field spectrum. This shows that the non-equilibrium Green's functions approach provides a versatile framework for exploring and analyzing field emission of correlated electrons.
